user.title: Roost
user.description: Roost plans your Weheat heat pump's thermostat 24 hours ahead on price, weather and the heat your house stores. It starts in shadow mode: it only shows what it would do.

data.name: Name
data.thermostat: Thermostat that drives the heat pump
data.room_temperature: Room temperature sensor (optional, better than the thermostat's)
data.import_weheat_history: Import the heat pump's history from Weheat now

data_description.heat_pump: The device of the official Weheat integration. Its sensors are found automatically.
data_description.thermostat: Roost only changes this thermostat's target temperature, like you would. The heat pump must follow the thermostat (not its own heating curve).
data_description.price_mode: Dynamic: a sensor with hourly prices. Fixed: you enter your contract's rate (and a low rate if you have one) in the next step.
data_description.import_price: Only with a dynamic price. A sensor with prices for the coming hours in its attributes (Nord Pool, ENTSO-e, Frank Energie, evcc, …). Without a forecast every hour costs the same.
data_description.export_price: Leave empty with net metering: export is then worth the import price.
data_description.import_weheat_history: Read-only, through the login of your Weheat integration: up to 13 months of hourly logs (heat, electricity, states), so Roost knows your house and heat pump from day one. Takes a few minutes.

data_description.fixed_price: All in: energy, taxes and VAT, as on your bill.
data_description.fixed_low_price: Leave empty with a single rate.
data_description.low_weekend: Many double-rate meters count the whole weekend as low.
data_description.fixed_export_price: Leave empty with net metering: export is then worth the import price.

data.grid_preference: Preference for own energy (added per kWh from the grid)

data_description.grid_power: All optional. With solar, Roost sees real solar surplus (export minus battery discharge, at most the solar power).
data_description.battery_power: Needed to tell solar export from a battery selling to the grid.
data_description.weather_source: Open-Meteo needs no account and gives radiation and wind (the house model uses both).

data.max_above_room: Setpoint at most this above the room
data.pause_hours: Pause after a change by hand
data.baseline_night: Night setback of the thermostat to compare with (0 = none)

data_description.store_max: Roost stores heat in the floor when an hour is cheap (or solar earns little) and an expensive one follows. Set it equal to the comfort temperature to switch that off.
data_description.max_above_room: Keeps an OpenTherm thermostat asking for lukewarm water (high COP).
data_description.baseline_night: The saving is shown against a steady thermostat at the comfort temperature, the usual advice for heat pumps.

error.not_weheat: This device has no Weheat heat pump sensors.
error.comfort_below_min: The comfort temperature must be at least the day minimum.
error.store_below_comfort: Storing heat must allow at least the comfort temperature.
error.day_order: The comfort hours must end after they start.
error.price_needed: Choose a price sensor, or choose a fixed price.

abort.already_configured: This heat pump is already set up.

not_following.title: {name}: the heat pump does not follow the thermostat
not_following.description: The heat pump has been heating for over 45 minutes while the thermostat asks for no heat. It probably runs on its own heating curve. Set it to follow the thermostat (in the Weheat app), otherwise Roost cannot steer it.

room_missing.title: {name}: no room temperature
room_missing.description: Neither the room sensor nor the thermostat has reported a room temperature for 30 minutes. Roost does not plan without it.

weheat_missing.title: {name}: Weheat heat pump not found
weheat_missing.description: The Weheat heat pump's sensors are not available. Check that the Weheat integration works.

learning_failed.title: {name}: learning failed
learning_failed.description: Roost could not learn from the history this time. It keeps using the previous model. The log has the details.

ready_for_active.title: {name}: ready to steer the heat pump

confirm.title: Switch to active
confirm.description:
Roost has checked its plan against the last {days} days: with the setpoints that were really on the thermostat it predicts the room {rmse} °C close 6 hours ahead, over {hours} heating hours, and the heat pump follows the thermostat.

Submit to let Roost steer the thermostat (mode active). You can go back to shadow at any time with the Roost mode selector.

suggest_raise_comfort.title: {name}: a little warmer during the day?

confirm.title: Raise the comfort temperature
confirm.description:
In the last two weeks the thermostat was turned up by hand during the comfort hours on {days} days ({count} times).

Submit to raise the comfort temperature from {current} to {value} °C. Ignore this if it was a one-off.

suggest_lower_comfort.title: {name}: a little cooler during the day?

confirm.title: Lower the comfort temperature
confirm.description:
In the last two weeks the thermostat was turned down by hand during the comfort hours on {days} days ({count} times).

Submit to lower the comfort temperature from {current} to {value} °C — that also saves energy.

confirm.title: Start the comfort hours earlier
confirm.description:
In the last two weeks the thermostat was turned up by hand shortly before the comfort hours on {days} days ({count} times).

Submit to start the comfort hours at {value} instead of {current}.

confirm.title: End the comfort hours later
confirm.description:
In the last two weeks the thermostat was turned up by hand shortly after the comfort hours on {days} days ({count} times).

Submit to end the comfort hours at {value} instead of {current}.

confirm.title: End the comfort hours earlier
confirm.description:
In the last two weeks the thermostat was turned down by hand near the end of the comfort hours on {days} days ({count} times).

Submit to end the comfort hours at {value} instead of {current} — that also saves energy.

pause.name: Pause
pause.description: Leave the thermostat alone for a while.

resume.name: Resume
resume.description: End a pause and plan again.

import_history.name: Import history from Weheat
import_history.description: Read the heat pump's hourly history from Weheat (read-only) and learn from it.
